issue.title: Cut a sase-core release containing 23f19f0 and raise the sase-core-rs floor before the next sase release
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-zu.8.5 (epic sase-zu.8, acceptance) as PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP notes #5 and #6; filed by sase-zu.8.land on 2026-09-13.

The published dependency floor lags the pinned cohort: pyproject.toml allows sase-core-rs>=0.34.23, but schema-30 index / scan-wire-9 support exists only at pin 23f19f0 (current sase-core-revision.txt pin 7f43a996 is its direct child), which no release tag contains — the newest release commit is v0.34.24 (782dc74), which predates 23f19f0.

`just check`'s core-floor probe reports blocked_unpublished: published 0.34.23 lacks artifact_ref_link_location_wire_schema_version and artifact_ref_split_link_location (from 17947a0) plus continuation_decide_resume_adoption and continuation_plan_retention (from 23f19f0). This is non-blocking for local/dev gates (probe exits 0) because dev installs build sase-core from the pinned checkout.

Remediation: cut a sase-core release containing 23f19f0 (or later), wait for the sase-core-rs wheel to publish, then raise the pyproject.toml floor through tools/ratchet_core_window. A sase release MUST NOT ship before this lands, otherwise a PyPI install pairs sase with a binding missing the sase-zu.8 machine-parity and index-completeness fixes.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP from sase-zr.7.1.1.5.4.1 note #1, independently rechecked 2026-09-19 while landing sase-zr.7.1.1.5.4: PyPI latest sase-core-rs is still 0.34.48 with 3 wheels and no sdist; 0.34.50 and later JSON endpoints 404. pyproject.toml/uv.lock remain >=0.34.48,<0.35.0. This epic removed the Python post_response_failure fallback and tools/validate_sase_core_rs now requires decide_gate_lifecycle to preserve that field, so a wheel install against the incomplete 0.34.48 floor cannot satisfy the released gate-decision contract. payload.entry: Corroboration from sase-13t.6 (2026-09-20): sase-core-rs 0.34.70 is now published COMPLETE on PyPI (5 files: manylinux_2_28 x86_64+aarch64, macOS universal2, win_amd64, sdist; none yanked; twine check clean, smoke tests green on linux/macos/windows in Release-plz run 35528969349). 0.34.48 is also complete (5 files). Tags v0.34.49-0.34.65 remain intentionally unpublished; 0.34.66-0.34.70 are complete. Commits 23f19f0, 4a8c6d4, 9bf272e, 9e1ab3f, 09f543b and 0a7301c are all ancestors of v0.34.70, so the blocker on published core is gone. tools/ratchet_core_window --report-only now proposes 0.34.48 -> 0.34.70 (>=0.34.70,<0.35.0). Raising the sase pin floor is NOT done here: it is sase-10d owned work via tools/ratchet_core_window.

ESCALATION from sase-13t.land (2026-09-20): this bead's remediation is now repairing a live breakage, not just preventing a future one. **Every published `sase` on PyPI is currently uninstallable.**

Cause: epic sase-13t's PyPI retention run deleted every `sase-core-rs` release below 0.34.23 to get the project back under its 10 GiB quota. The surviving set is 0.34.23-0.34.48 plus 0.34.66-0.34.70 (31 releases, 155 files, 2.27 GB). But the newest published `sase` is 0.17.1, and its frozen PyPI metadata pins `sase-core-rs>=0.32.16,<0.33.0` — a window with nothing left in it. The epic's pin audit (note #1 on sase-13t.1) grepped the consumer *checkouts* for pins and correctly found nothing below 0.34.19; it did not check the requirement metadata already frozen into the consumers' *published* distributions, which is where this one lives.

Reproduced 2026-09-20 with `uv pip compile` against live PyPI:

- `sase==0.17.1` -> `No solution found ... Because only sase-core-rs>=0.34.23 is available and sase==0.17.1 depends on sase-core-rs>=0.32.16,<0.33.0, we can conclude that sase==0.17.1 cannot be used.` Every published `sase` (0.13.3 through 0.17.1) carries the same `<0.33.0` window.
- `sase-research-artifacts` -> hard resolution failure (it pins `sase-core-rs>=0.34.23,<0.35.0`, which cannot coexist with any installable `sase`).
- `sase-telegram` -> "succeeds" only by backtracking to `sase-telegram==0.4.9` with `sase==0.1.0`; `sase-github` likewise lands on `sase-github==0.1.0` with `sase==0.1.0`. A silent year-old downgrade rather than an error, which is arguably worse.

Deletion is irreversible — PyPI permanently burns a deleted version and never accepts a re-upload of the filename — so the 0.32.x window cannot be restored. **Publishing a `sase` release whose floor is a surviving core version is the only remedy**, which is exactly this bead. Core is ready for it: 0.34.70 is published complete (5 unyanked files) and contains 23f19f0, and `tools/ratchet_core_window --report-only` proposes 0.34.48 -> 0.34.70.

Note for whoever works this: `sase-telegram`'s `uv.lock` still has a transitive `sase-core-rs 0.32.61` entry, which is now a deleted version (recorded as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on sase-13t.1). It cannot be refreshed in place, because `uv lock --upgrade-package sase-core-rs` would keep `sase` at 0.17.1 and there is no core version left in that package's window. It resolves on its own once a `sase` release with the new floor is published; nothing in that repo reads the lock today (no `uv sync`, `--locked`, or `--frozen` in its Justfile, workflows, or scripts), so it is not currently breaking anything.

This bead was already READY and already said a `sase` release must not ship before it lands. Nothing about its remediation changes; only its urgency does.

payload.description: Epic sase-13t's PyPI retention deletion removed every sase-core-rs 0.32.x release, which is the window every published sase pins; this bead's floor raise plus a sase release is the only way to make 'pip install sase' resolve again.
